strings.title: Adding Integers
strings.label: Day 1
strings.strategy: Adding a negative moves down; adding a positive moves up. Jump to zero first when you cross it, or make zero pairs.
strings.keywords: integers, positive, negative, zero, zero pairs, jump through zero, vertical number line
watchFor: Adding the digits and keeping the first sign (-25 + 40 = -65): ask "Do you go up or down from −25? How far?"
Thinking two negatives make a positive when adding: ask "Owing 8 and owing 3 more: how much do you owe?"
Losing track crossing zero: ask "How far is −63 from 0? Then how much is left of the 48?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "How did zero help?" Land: jump to zero first, then use what's left. Adding a negative moves down; adding a positive moves up.

problems.notes: Look for: down 3 from 8. Ask: "Hold on to this." Word choice: "adding a negative". Model: vline 8 -3
Look for: up 3 from −8. Ask: "What's the same as the last one? What's different?" Model: vline -8 +3

responses.tip: Ask: from −8, going up 3, do you reach zero?

problems.notes: Look for: down 3 more from −8. Ask: "Up or down?" Model: vline -8 -3

responses.tip: Ask: owing 8 and owing 3 more: how much do you owe?

problems.notes: Look for: 25 up to 0, 15 more. Ask: "Where does zero help?" Model: vline -25 +25 +15

responses.tip: Through zero.
Added the numbers, kept the sign. Ask: up or down from −25?

problems.notes: Look for: up 48 doesn't reach zero: −15. Ask: "Do you get to zero?" Model: numberline -63 +48

responses.tip: Right size, wrong side. Ask: is 48 enough to get from −63 to 0?

problems.notes: Look for: down 120 to 0, 55 more. Ask: "Up or down? Past zero?" Model: numberline 120 -120 -55
Look for: up 2.5 to 0, 2.25 more. Ask: "Same moves with decimals?" Model: vline -2.5 +2.5 +2.25

strings.title: Subtracting Integers as Distance
strings.label: Day 2
strings.strategy: a − b is the jump from b to a: how far, and which way. Up is positive, down is negative. 12 − (−5) is the jump from −5 up to 12.
strings.keywords: difference, distance, from, to, up, down, vertical number line, thermometer
watchFor: Treating − − as "just subtract" (12 − −5 = 7): ask "How far is it from −5 to 12?"
Right distance, wrong direction (−30 − −45 = −15): ask "From −45 to −30, up or down?"
Seeing a double negative where there isn't one (45 − 72): ask "Is 72 negative?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "How does 'from the second number to the first' help?" Land: a − b is the jump from b to a. Up is positive, down is negative. Through zero, add the two parts.

problems.notes: Look for: from −5 up to 0 is 5, then 12 more. Ask: "How far from −5 to 12?" Word choice: "from −5 to 12". Model: vline -5 >0 >12

responses.tip: The target strategy.
Ask: how far is it from −5 to 12 on the thermometer?

problems.notes: Look for: from 5 down to −12: 17 down. Ask: "Up or down?" Model: vline 5 -5 -12

responses.tip: Taking away 5. Also fine.

problems.notes: Look for: from −5 down to −12: 7 down. Ask: "Is −12 above or below −5?" Model: vline -5 -7

responses.tip: Right distance, wrong direction. Ask: from −5 to −12, up or down?

problems.notes: Look for: from −45 up to −30: 15. Ask: "Which is higher?" Model: vline -45 >-30

responses.tip: Ask: from −45 to −30, up or down?

problems.notes: Look for: from 72 down to 45: 27 down. Ask: "Is there a double negative here?" Model: vline 72 -27

responses.tip: Ask: is the answer above or below zero if you take 72 from 45?

problems.notes: Look for: from 2.5 down to −1.5: 2.5 to 0, 1.5 more. Ask: "Same with decimals?" Model: vline 2.5 -2.5 -1.5
Look for: from −37 down to −100: 63 down. Ask: "How far apart are they?" Model: vline -37 -63

strings.title: Bigger Integer Products and Quotients
strings.label: Day 3
strings.strategy: Work out the size with a mental math strategy (double and halve, a friendly factor), then decide the sign: same signs positive, different signs negative.
strings.keywords: integers, product, quotient, sign, double and halve, friendly factor
watchFor: Getting the size right but the sign wrong: ask "Same signs or different signs?"
Doing the sign first and getting lost in the calculation: ask "Ignore the signs: what's 25 × 16?"
With decimals (−48 ÷ −1.2), losing the place: ask "How many 1.2s in 48? About how many?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "How did you split the work?" Land: size first, with your best mental strategy; sign second, from the rule. Two separate questions.

problems.notes: Look for: 25 × 16 = 100 × 4, then the sign. Ask: "Size first, then sign?" Word choice: "same signs, different signs". Model: halve 25 x 16 = 50 x 8 = 100 x 4

responses.tip: Size by double and halve, then the sign.
Size right, sign wrong. Ask: same signs or different signs?

problems.notes: Look for: 12 × 15 = 6 × 30. Ask: "Same signs?" Model: halve 12 x 15 = 6 x 30
Look for: 8 and half of 8. Ask: "Does the rule change with decimals?" Model: area 1+0.5 x 8
Look for: half of 36. Ask: "Same signs?" Model: bar 1/2 of 36

responses.tip: Ask: two negatives multiplied: same signs or different?

problems.notes: Look for: 480 ÷ 12. Ask: "How many 1.2s in 48?" Model: text -48 ÷ -1.2 = 480 ÷ 12 ; = 40

responses.tip: Scale both by 10.
Ask: 4 × 1.2 is 4.8. Is that 48?

problems.notes: Look for: 125 × 8 = 1000. Ask: "What do you know about 125?" Model: halve 125 x 8 = 250 x 4 = 500 x 2

strings.title: Order of Operations with Integers
strings.label: Day 4
strings.strategy: Brackets first, then multiplication and division, then addition and subtraction. Pairs of problems that differ only by brackets show why the order matters.
strings.keywords: order of operations, brackets, multiply first, integers, sign
watchFor: Working left to right (−3 + 4 × −2 = −2): ask "Which operation comes first?"
Dropping the sign after multiplying (20 − 3 × −4 = 20 − 12): ask "What is 3 × −4? What does subtracting a negative do?"
Ignoring brackets: ask "What do the brackets tell you to do first?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "Why did each pair have different answers?" Land: the brackets changed what happens first. Multiplication and division come before addition and subtraction, unless brackets say otherwise.

problems.notes: Look for: 4 × −2 = −8 first, then −3 + −8. Ask: "Which comes first?" Word choice: "multiply first". Model: text 4 x -2 = -8 ; -3 + -8 = -11

responses.tip: Multiply first.
Worked left to right. Ask: which operation comes first?

problems.notes: Look for: brackets first: 1 × −2. Ask: "What changed?" Model: text -3 + 4 = 1 ; 1 x -2 = -2

responses.tip: Brackets change the order.
Lost the negative. Ask: what is 3 × −4?

problems.notes: Look for: 17 × −4. Ask: "Brackets first?" Model: text 20 - 3 = 17 ; 17 x -4 = -68
Look for: −12 ÷ 3 = −4, then −4 + 5. Ask: "Divide first?" Model: text -12 ÷ 3 = -4 ; -4 + 5 = 1
Look for: −12 ÷ 8. Ask: "What do the brackets do this time?" Model: text 3 + 5 = 8 ; -12 ÷ 8 = -1.5

responses.tip: Ignored the brackets. Ask: what do the brackets tell you to do first?

strings.connection: Day 3: Bigger Integer Products and Quotients

strings.title: Choosing an Integer Strategy, Round 2
strings.label: Day 5
strings.strategy: All four operations with integers, mixed. Decide the operation, think about direction or sign, then use a friendly strategy for the size.
strings.keywords: integers, add, subtract, multiply, divide, sign, direction, distance
watchFor: Using the multiplication sign rule for addition (−7 + −9 = 16): ask "Is it adding or multiplying?"
Subtracting as distance in the wrong direction: ask "From which number to which?"
Not checking reasonableness: ask "Should the answer be positive or negative? Big or small?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "How did you decide the sign each time?" Land: adding and subtracting are about direction on the number line; multiplying and dividing use same signs/different signs. Size comes from your best mental strategy.

problems.notes: Look for: down 9 from −7. Ask: "Adding or multiplying?" Model: vline -7 -9

responses.tip: Used the multiplication rule. Ask: is it adding or multiplying?

problems.notes: Look for: same signs, 63. Ask: "What changed?" Model: text 7 x 9 = 63 ; same signs: 63
Look for: from −15 up to 15. Ask: "How far apart?" Model: vline -15 >0 >15
Look for: 84 ÷ 7 = 12, different signs. Ask: "Which strategy fits these numbers?" Model: text 7 x 12 = 84 ; -84 ÷ 7 = -12
Look for: up 50 to 0, 75 more. Ask: "Which strategy fits these numbers?" Model: vline -50 +50 +75
Look for: −4 × 2.5 = −10, × −3 = 30. Ask: "Which pair first?" Model: text -4 x 2.5 = -10 ; -10 x -3 = 30

responses.tip: Pick the friendly pair first.
Ask: how many negatives? Even or odd?

problems.notes: Look for: −10 × −5 = 50. Ask: "Brackets first?" Model: text -6 + -4 = -10 ; 3 - 8 = -5 ; -10 x -5 = 50

strings.connection: Week 3 · Day 5: Choosing an Integer Strategy
